action: If you installed or updated the Claude Code extension to 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 from Cursor's marketplace on October 29, follow Cursor's October 30 notice (uninstalling alone may not be enough) and rotate any keys Cursor or Fireworks flagged.
attack: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
exec: A supplier's leaked key led to tampered developer tools reaching up to 5,000 users; Cursor has dropped the supplier for inference.
plain: Coding-tool maker Cursor says a key it gave supplier Fireworks AI was exposed. Attackers used it to copy data, then posted harmful copies of a popular add-on for about 11 hours on October 29, reaching at most 5,000 users.

key_findings: An attacker used an access key Cursor had issued to Fireworks AI, which Fireworks exposed, to copy data from a read-only storage bucket.
The bucket held coding agent traces, mostly from 2025, from sessions not in Privacy Mode; under 0.01% of customers had API credentials exposed.
Credentials in those traces opened some SaaS tools, archived non-production repositories, limited support data and usage metrics.
On October 29 malicious copies of the Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313, sat in the marketplace cache for about 11 hours; at most 5,000 users could have received them.
Cursor saw the last attacker activity on November 1 and moved all inference off Fireworks; Fireworks' own bulletin dates its first intrusion to August 3 to October 7.
recommendations: If you installed or updated to Claude Code extension 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 during the window, follow Cursor's October 30 security notice; uninstalling alone may not be enough.
Rotate any exposed keys; admins were sent lists of affected keys.
Fireworks customers: create new API keys, rotate third-party credentials named in your notice and review access logs for those credentials.

summary: Cursor's November 13 update says an access key it had issued to Fireworks AI was exposed by that supplier and used to copy coding agent traces from a read-only bucket. Credentials found in the traces opened further internal tools. On October 29 the attacker placed malicious Claude Code extension builds 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 in Cursor's marketplace cache for about 11 hours; at most 5,000 users could have received them.
title: Cursor says stolen Fireworks AI key led to trojanized Claude Code extension

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Cursor report.

review.note: Compared Cursor Nov 13 post (key exposed by Fireworks, 2.1.312/2.1.313, 11 hours, at most 5,000 users, under 0.01%) with Hacker News and Fireworks bulletins
